Greetings and directions on the street
Say good morning, tell someone where you're going and ask the way to Hibari Mart.
Talk to a neighbour on the street
Say good morning and chat about the weather
Ask for directions and understand them
Say thank you and goodbye
Speaking practice with the microphone (optional)
Good morning! Lovely morning, isn't it?
Good morning.
Morning.
Good evening.
Heh, "ohayou" is for friends. With neighbours, say "ohayou gozaimasu".
"Konbanwa" is an evening greeting. It's morning now, so try again.
Nice weather today, isn't it?
Yes, it really is lovely weather.
Yes, it's weather.
No, it's raining.
Right. "Sou desu ne" (it is, isn't it) sounds more natural.
Huh? It isn't raining. Look up at the sky.
Where are you off to?
I'm going to Hibari Mart.
The convenience store.
I go convenience store.
The convenience store. "Konbini e ikimasu" is easier to understand.
Not "wo" but "e". "Konbini e ikimasu". Say it again.
Hibari Mart, I see. But it's your first time in this area, isn't it?
Yes, it's my first time. Where is the convenience store?
Convenience store, where?
Is it a convenience store?
Heh. Let's say "konbini wa doko desu ka", that's more polite.
Huh? I'm the one asking you. To ask where something is, say "~ wa doko desu ka". Try again.
Go straight along this road.
Then turn right at the next corner. It's the shop with the red roof.
Did you get that? Where is Hibari Mart?
Go straight and then turn right, right?
Sorry, could you say that once more, please?
I don't understand.
Go straight and then turn left, right?
Sure. I'll say it slowly. Go straight... then turn right.
Not left. It's right, the side you hold your chopsticks with.
That's right! Well done.
Hibari Mart has really good onigiri.
Thank you very much.
Thanks.
Goodbye.
You're welcome. With neighbours, "arigatou gozaimasu" is more polite.
"Sayounara" sounds a bit sad. First say "arigatou gozaimasu".
Take care. Have a nice trip.
Excuse me, I'll be going.
See you later.
Hello.
Heh, "jaa ne" is for friends. "Shitsurei shimasu" is polite.
"Konnichiwa" is a greeting for when you meet. When parting, say "shitsurei shimasu".
Speaking practice (optional): press V and say this sentence out loud to practise your pronunciation.
Summary: "~ e ikimasu" (go to ~) and "~ wa doko desu ka" (where is ~?). Direction words: massugu (straight), migi (right), hidari (left). Now head to Hibari Mart!
